name: Chloe Ferro

education.notes: Studied at Tulane University in the US before joining the family-adjacent digital health world.

keyDecisions: Took a product/marketing role at a consumer digital-health-adjacent company before founding — first commercial reps.
lessons: Working at a fast-moving consumer-adjacent insurance/healthtech business teaches commercial mechanics that pure-MBA paths don't.

keyDecisions: Co-founded SheMed in April 2024 with her sister Olivia Ferro — sibling team built on a shared digital-health background.
Picked the women's-GLP-1 wedge — overlaying medical advice, data and personalised support on the weight-management protocol.
Scaled from launch to $1B valuation in ~18 months — among the fastest UK healthtech unicorn trajectories on record.
lessons: Founder pairs from a domain-adjacent family/early-career base can move faster than first-principles founders — they pre-skip the customer-discovery cycle.
Specific demographic (women) + specific intervention (GLP-1 + monitoring) is a sharper wedge than generic health-tech.
Healthcare unicorn velocity is achievable in the UK when the buyer is the direct consumer (not the NHS) and the willingness-to-pay is regulatory-tailwind (GLP-1 demand spike).
careerSteps.notes: SheMed founded April 2024. $50M Series A October 2025 → $1B unicorn valuation. Chloe is President; sister Olivia is CEO. Forbes 30 Under 30 Europe 2026 (Science & Healthcare).

outcomes.currentStatus: Co-Founder & President of SheMed (London); $1B unicorn after $50M Series A in October 2025. Pre-exit; paper wealth.

lessons.lesson: Sibling co-founder pair with a shared digital-health background can compress customer-discovery vs. first-principles founders.
Women's GLP-1 weight-management is a high-willingness-to-pay consumer wedge with a regulatory tailwind.
Found at 22 with the right partner + the right wedge — age is not the constraint, market timing is.
